[agent-bulk] numucc_em. Vertex judged first and it is FINE: at el+60 the star is a clear multi-prong fan -- the 248 cm muon (15006) one way, and the 45019/46032/47033 prongs off the same point. shw 45019 (228.2 MeV, 5 seg, 60.2 cm, conn 3) is the leading pdg-11 object and I cannot settle it. What is certain from the numbers and visible on the acceptance plot: EVERY member except the seed sits at 44-58 deg from the shower axis, above all three pass-1 dashed steps (15/20/30 deg), and 45031 (4.9 cm) is at 106.1 deg, i.e. behind the start; they were pulled in by in_other_clusters_A (walk_add), not by the cone. Two non-members, 48034 (0.9 cm) at 11.4 cm/58.5 deg and 41012 (1.6 cm) at 23.3 cm/68.7 deg, sit interleaved with the members at the same angles. Reading (a), which I lean to slightly and is why the verdict says over-clustered: the member set spans two directions -- at az+085 the skeleton goes up from the X, turns, and comes back down -- so at least one arm (45031 at 106 deg is the concrete candidate) does not belong. Reading (b), which I cannot rule out and may be the truer statement: the membership is fine and what is wrong is the SHOWER START and AXIS -- at az-055 the X sits in the MIDDLE of one continuous ~39 cm curving body and the orange axis arrow points roughly perpendicular to it, which by itself manufactures every one of those 44-106 deg numbers. The verdict vocabulary has no 'start/axis wrong' entry and vertex-bad is about the nu vertex, which is good here, so this is recorded as the closest available string. NO segment marks: as in the pilot's evt280159 I could not name which pieces to remove with confidence. Also unowned and contiguous with the body: 45030 (pdg 211, 15.5 cm, same cluster 45) at 13.8 cm/125.1 deg. Not judged: 46032 (309.3 MeV but pdg 2212, one 53.7 cm segment -- a range-converted proton track, higher kine_best than the EM object) and 47033 (96.8 MeV, pdg 2212, only 7.4 cm -- also a range-converted proton stub); 15006 is the muon. 15 further showers skipped by the scope rule, all under 20 MeV. No pi0 group and only one EM shower in scope, so nothing to pair.
